"'''Prithibi Ta Naki Chhoto Hote Hote'''" (Bengali:{{Lang|bn|পৃথিবীটা নাকি ছোট হতে হতে}} {{Literal translation|Our world keeps shrinking|lk=yes}}) is a [[Bengali Rock music (India)|Bengali rock]] song by [[Krosswindz]] from [[Moheener Ghoraguli]]'s 1995 album ''[[Aabaar Bochhor Kuri Pore]]''. It was composed and written by [[Gautam Chattopadhyay]], and sung by [[Bonnie Chakraborty]]. This song among others in the album helped ''Moheener Ghoraguli'' in their way to popularity and critical recognition after they disbanded in 1981. It was later covered by various Bengali rock bands and also in a [[Hindi film music|Hindi song]] called "[[Bheegi Bheegi]]".

== Background ==
A decade-and-a-half after ''[[Moheener Ghoraguli]]'' (MG), the Bengali rock band, disbanded in 1981 was when the lead composer of the band, [[Gautam Chattopadhyay]], decided to create a new album after being fascinated by the [[MTV]] music videos that were released in the early 90s. Chattopadhyay's son, [[Gourab Chatterjee|Gaurab Chatterjee]], in an interview stated, "He (Gautam) got new people to sing some of his post-Moheener songs, shot videos for them and that’s how a collective of great music came about".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sethu |first=Divya |title=In the 1970s, India's First Rock Band Was Born In The Backyard of A Kolkata Home |url=https://thebetterindia.com/257125/moheener-ghoraguli-indias-first-rock-band-bengali-music-bollywood-commercial-songs-gautam-chattopadhya-gaurab-chatterjee-kolkata-music-history-div200/ |access-date=2026-06-19 |website=thebetterindia.com |language=en |archive-date=2025-12-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251216120523/https://thebetterindia.com/257125/moheener-ghoraguli-indias-first-rock-band-bengali-music-bollywood-commercial-songs-gautam-chattopadhya-gaurab-chatterjee-kolkata-music-history-div200/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The album, ''[[Aabaar Bochhor Kuri Pore]],'' would include songs from artists other than MG namely [[Krosswindz]], [[Lakkhichhara]], Garer Maath and individual artists for e.g., [[Surojit Chatterjee]], [[Antara Chowdhury]] and [[Paroma Banerji]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=20 and counting: A score of ways the number shapes our lives |url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/west-bengal/kolkata/20-and-counting-a-score-of-ways-the-number-shapes-our-lives-prnt/cid/2116998 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250911184426/https://www.telegraphindia.com/west-bengal/kolkata/20-and-counting-a-score-of-ways-the-number-shapes-our-lives-prnt/cid/2116998 |archive-date=2025-09-11 |access-date=2026-06-19 |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref> One of the songs from the album, ''Prithibi Ta Naki Chhoto Hote Hote'', was a collaborative work between Krosswindz and MG.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Dsouza |first=Krystelle |title=10 Rare Pics: A Raga Reaches Outer Space, India's First Rock Band & More |url=https://thebetterindia.com/326955/rare-pics-of-milestones-and-historic-moments-of-india-music-history/ |access-date=2026-06-19 |website=thebetterindia.com |language=en |archive-date=2024-01-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240114165702/https://www.thebetterindia.com/326955/rare-pics-of-milestones-and-historic-moments-of-india-music-history/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Release and reception ==
The song with the album, ''Aabaar Bochhor Kuri Pore,'' was released as a booklet in [[Kolkata Book Fair]] in January 1995. [[Fossils (band)|Fossils]]' lead guitarist [[Allan Ao]] understood the lyrics much later than the song's release as he found the wordplay in the lyrics to be "fantastic" and that "It has taken on an anthemic quality, both young and old listeners love it."<ref>{{Cite news |title=Mohiner Ghoraguli, Cactus, Lakkhichhara: Fossils' Allan Temjen Ao picks favourites |url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/my-kolkata/people/mohiner-ghoraguli-cactus-lakkhichhara-fossils-allan-temjen-ao-picks-favourites/cid/1833348 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250824113741/https://www.telegraphindia.com/my-kolkata/people/mohiner-ghoraguli-cactus-lakkhichhara-fossils-allan-temjen-ao-picks-favourites/cid/1833348 |archive-date=2025-08-24 |access-date=2026-06-19 |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref> This was the first hit Bengali rock song as stated by Lakkhichhara's drummer Gaboo (or Gaurab Chatterjee),{{Efn|Not to be confused with Gautam Chattopadhyay's son}} "The first hit rock number was ''Prithibi ta naki chhoto hote hote'', composed by Gautam Chatterjee in 1995 and performed by Krosswindz in ''Abar Bochhor Kuri Porey''."<ref>{{Cite news |date=2017-08-25 |title=Who really owns Bangla rock? |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/bengali/music/who-really-owns-bangla-rock/articleshow/60218976.cms |access-date=2026-06-19 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257 |archive-date=2024-11-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241127213612/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/bengali/music/who-really-owns-bangla-rock/articleshow/60218976.cms |url-status=live }}</ref>

Critical commentary remarked in the deeper meaning within the song's lyrics as being "one of the most celebrated anthems for the doomed youth of [[technocracy]]". It is stated that the song's narrator remained conscious of the [[Ontology|ontologically]] [[Liminality|liminal]] person, which is a result of technocracy and remaining immobile for a period of time.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alternative Music, Youth and the Politic {{!}} CCYSC |url=https://www.theccysc.com/alternative-music-youth-and-politics |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220308041737/https://www.theccysc.com/alternative-music-youth-and-politics |archive-date=2022-03-08 |access-date=2026-06-19 |website=CCYSC |language=en}}</ref> The narrator is both ridiculing and inquisitive to the "alienated selves of the urban [[Bengalis|Bengali]] middle class".<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Chattopadhyay |first=Shankhadeep |date=2021-06-30 |title=Spatializing the Musicking Of an Expressive Urban Imagination: A Trans-Cultural Evaluation of the Early-Modern Rock Music of Bengal |url=http://rupkatha.com/v13n251/ |journal=Rupkatha Journal on Interdisciplinary Studies in Humanities |volume=13 |issue=2 |doi=10.21659/rupkatha.v13n2.51 |issn=0975-2935 |doi-access=free |archive-date=2023-12-03 |access-date=2026-06-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231203010500/https://rupkatha.com/v13n251/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The modern society is being rendered to a state of being alone together for which marvels of technology such as telephones and television are among the ones to be held responsible. The song concludes by saying that the stars that are [[light-year]]s away are closer to us than our loved ones "because one can see stars far more easily than their dear ones".<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Chakravarty |first=Devpriya |date=2024-05-08 |title=Exploring the Socio-Musical Legacy of Moheener Ghoraguli, the Progressive Rock Pioneers of Bengal |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/19401159.2024.2346996 |journal=Rock Music Studies |language=EN |doi=10.1080/19401159.2024.2346996#d1e266 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240621081219/https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/19401159.2024.2346996 |archive-date=2024-06-21 |hdl=10072/430773 |hdl-access=free |access-date=2026-06-19 |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Other versions ==
In the 2006 [[Hindi cinema|Bollywood]] film, [[Gangster: A Love Story|Gangster]], a song "[[Bheegi Bheegi]]" was released which was originally composed by [[Mayur Puri]] and sung by [[James (musician)|James]], and it was adapted from the song by ''Moheener Ghoraguli''.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite book |last=Arunachalam |first=Param |url=https://www.google.co.in/books/edition/BollySwar_2001_2010/UNvyDwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=prithibi+ta+naki+chhoto+hote+hote&pg=PA611-IA1&printsec=frontcover |title=BollySwar: 2001 - 2010 |publisher=Mavrix Infotech Private Limited |isbn=978-81-938482-0-3 |language=en}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
In a tribute to ''Moheener Ghoraguli'' in 2013, the [[Tollywood (Bengali cinema)|Tollywood]] film ''[[Hanuman.com]],'' included the song and was remarked by the protagonist [[Prosenjit Chatterjee]] as, "The more I hear the lyrics, I realize how Goutam Chattopadhyay acted as a pathbreaker by composing a prophetic number ''Prithibita naki chhoto hote hote''. The song has given life to the film."<ref>{{Cite news |date=2013-11-30 |title=Prithibi ta naki was a pathbreaker for Bangla rock music: Prosenjit Chatterjee |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/bengali/music/prithibi-ta-naki-was-a-pathbreaker-for-bangla-rock-music-prosenjit-chatterjee/articleshow/26474862.cms |access-date=2026-06-19 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257 |archive-date=2016-11-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161117050746/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/bengali/music/Prithibi-ta-naki-was-a-pathbreaker-for-Bangla-rock-music-Prosenjit-Chatterjee/articleshow/26474862.cms |url-status=live }}</ref>

In November 2023, [[Coca-Cola|Coca Cola]] organised a two–day event in Kolkata which included music performances by artists such as Fossils , Lakkhichhara, [[Euphoria (Indian band)|Euphoria]], [[When Chai Met Toast]], [[Amit Trivedi]], [[Coke Studio Bangla]] etc. Coke Studio Bangla paid tribute to MG by performing the song, ''Prithibi ta naki chhoto hote hote.''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Coca-Cola Kolkata Is Cooking was a magical medley of music and food. t2 was there to experience the fizzy fest |url=https://www.t2online.in/music/indian/coca-cola-kolkata-is-cooking-was-a-magical-medley-of-music-and-food.-t2-was-there-to-experience-the-fizzy-fest/658283 |access-date=2026-06-19 |website=www.t2online.in |language=en}}</ref>
